rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for asking which item or person is meant.

example.english: Tell me which book is yours.
example.traditional: 話畀我知邊本書係你嘅。
example.jyutping: waa6 bei2 ngo5 zi1 bin1 bun2 syu1 hai6 nei5 ge3

rows.note: Use this as the default bare question for which person or which one.

example.english: Which person do you want to invite to dinner?
example.jyutping: nei5 soeng2 ceng2 bin1 go3 sik6 faan6

rows.note: Use this when the selected thing is named with its classifier and noun, such as which book.

example.english: Which book do you think is the most useful?
example.jyutping: nei5 gok3 dak1 bin1 bun2 syu1 zeoi3 jau5 jung6

rows.note: Use this for a plural selection when several items are being chosen.

example.english: Which restaurants still have tables tonight?
example.jyutping: gam1 maan5 bin1 di1 caan1 teng1 zung6 jau5 wai2

rows.note: Use this free-choice construction when the meaning is whichever or any one that fits, rather than a question.

example.english: It doesn't matter which one you choose.
example.jyutping: nei5 gaan2 bin1 go3 dou1 dak1
